home.title: Welcome
home.noAccounts: You are not a member of any account yet
home.noAccountsHelp: Ask a platform administrator to add you to an account.

errors.access_denied: The login was cancelled or refused.
errors.provider_error: The identity provider reported an error.
errors.provider_unavailable: The identity provider cannot be reached. Try again later.
errors.login_expired: The login took too long or was interrupted. Please try again.
errors.login_failed: The login could not be completed.
errors.server_error: The login failed on the server. Please try again.
errors.oidc_disabled: Single sign-on is not set up here.

overview.description: What this account runs and stores.

workers.description: Deploy Workers with wrangler; manage them here.
workers.emptyHelp: Deploy one with `wrangler deploy`, pointed at this platform.
workers.versionsHelp: Every upload is a version. Deploy any of them, or split traffic between two.
workers.splitHelp: Send part of the requests to this version and the rest to another. Workers with Durable Objects or static assets cannot be split.
workers.bindingsHelp: What the Worker's code reaches through env, as of its current version.
workers.secretsHelp: Encrypted values the Worker reads from env. Changing one makes a new version.
workers.addSecretHelp: The value is encrypted and never shown again.
workers.workersDevHelp: The address every Worker gets under the account's subdomain.
workers.routesHelp: URL patterns in the account's zones that run this Worker.
workers.addRouteHelp: A pattern in one of the account's zones, such as example.com/api/*.
workers.addDomainHelp: The hostname must be in one of the account's zones.
workers.cronsHelp: Schedules that run the Worker's scheduled handler, in UTC.
workers.addCronHelp: A cron expression with five fields, such as */15 * * * *.
workers.removeTriggerConsequence: The Worker stops running for it. You can add it again later.

logs.title: Live logs
logs.help: Requests, console output and exceptions as they happen. The newest come first; the last 1,000 are kept.
logs.waitingHelp: Send the Worker a request and it shows up here.
logs.notRunning: Logs are stopped. Start them to watch the Worker.

kv.description: Key-value namespaces Workers read and write.
kv.emptyHelp: Create one here or with `wrangler kv namespace create`.
kv.binary: This value is binary ({{size}} bytes) and cannot be edited here.
kv.ttlHelp: Leave empty to keep the key. At least 60.
kv.ttlInvalid: A whole number of at least 60.
kv.metadataHelp: Up to 1,024 bytes, returned with the key. Leave empty for none.

d1.description: SQLite databases Workers query through D1.
d1.emptyHelp: Create one here or with `wrangler d1 create`.
d1.queryHelp: Statements run against the live database, one after another.
d1.exportHelp: Download the whole database as SQL statements.
d1.importHelp: Run a .sql file of statements against the database, as `wrangler d1 execute --file` does.

r2.description: Object storage buckets, reachable from Workers and over the S3 API.
r2.emptyHelp: Create one here or with `wrangler r2 bucket create`.
r2.nameRule: 3 to 63 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
r2.noObjectsHelp: Upload files, or write them from a Worker.
r2.deleteConsequence: This cannot be undone. Only an empty bucket can be deleted.
r2.publicAccessHelp: A public address that serves the bucket's objects to anyone.
r2.publicUrl: Serve objects at a public address
r2.customDomainsHelp: Your own hostnames serving the bucket's objects.
r2.addDomainHelp: The hostname must be in one of the account's zones.
r2.noZones: This account has no zones. A platform administrator assigns them.
r2.removeDomainConsequence: The hostname stops serving the bucket.
r2.lifecycleHelp: Rules that delete objects or abandon uploads after a time.
r2.lifecycleEditHelp: The rules as the API takes them: a JSON list.
r2.rulesInvalid: This is not a JSON list.
r2.notificationsHelp: Queues told about changes to objects. Set them up with `wrangler r2 bucket notification`.

queues.emptyHelp: Create one here or with `wrangler queues create`.
queues.sendHelp: Adds one message to the queue, as a producer would.
queues.purgeConsequence: This deletes every message waiting in the queue. It cannot be undone.

workflows.description: Durable, multi-step programs defined by Workers.
workflows.emptyHelp: Deploy a Worker with a `workflows` binding to create one.
workflows.instanceIdHelp: Leave empty for a random one.

durableObjects.description: Durable Object classes of the account's Workers.
durableObjects.emptyHelp: Deploy a Worker with a Durable Object binding and a migration.

containers.description: Container applications that Durable Objects start.
containers.emptyHelp: Deploy a Worker with `containers` in its wrangler configuration.
containers.disabledHelp: The platform runs without an image registry.
containers.rolloutsHelp: Each deploy that changes the application is a rollout, applied at once.

settings.membersHelp: People who log in with single sign-on and use this account.
settings.inviteHelp: Whoever logs in with this email, verified by the identity provider, becomes a member.
settings.removeMemberConsequence: They lose access to this account at once. Tokens they created keep working until revoked.
settings.groupHelp: Everyone in this identity-provider group is a member, without being added one by one.
settings.groupEditHelp: The group's name as the identity provider sends it. Leave empty for none.
settings.tokensHelp: For wrangler and other tools. A token can do everything in this account.
settings.tokensNeedPerson: Tokens are managed by people who log in with single sign-on, and by administrators.
settings.createTokenHelp: Name it after what will use it.
settings.creatorLeft: Creator is no longer a member
settings.tokenOnce: Copy it now: it is not shown again.
settings.wranglerSetup: For wrangler, with the platform's API address:
settings.s3Keys: For the S3 API, its access key ID and secret:
settings.revokeConsequence: Anything using it stops working at once.
settings.deleteAccountHelp: Deletes the account and everything in it: Workers, data, members and tokens.
settings.deleteAccountConsequence: This cannot be undone. Everything in {{name}} is deleted: Workers, KV, D1, R2, queues, members and tokens. Durable Object storage is left for the operator to remove.

admin.description: Accounts, people and zones of the whole platform.
admin.usersHelp: Everyone who has logged in with single sign-on.
admin.noUsers: Nobody has logged in with single sign-on yet
admin.removeUserConsequence: Their memberships and sessions end. If they log in again, they come back without memberships.
admin.zonesHelp: Domains assigned to accounts for routes and custom domains. Selvedge does not check who owns them.
admin.addZoneHelp: The account can then route hostnames in this domain to its Workers.
admin.removeZoneConsequence: Routes and custom domains in it stop working.
